newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan phosphates firm sells joint venture stake.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan phosphates firm sells joint venture stake.

text.p: Moroccan phosphates firm, Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP), said on Wednesday it had signed an agreement to sell to the German Chemische Fabrik Budenheim (CFB) a 20 percent stake of a joint venture with a Belgian company.

Under the agreement, the capital of Societe Euro-Maroc Phosphore (EMAPHOS) would be distributed with 40 percent going to OCP, 40 percent to the Belgian company Prayon-Rupel S.A. and 20 percent to CFB, OCP said in a statement.
EMAPHOS was established as a 50/50 joint venture between OCP and Prayon-Rupel S.A., the Belgian foam products maker, early this year.

OCP general manager Mourad Cherif, Prayon managing director Jean Leroy, and CFB general manager Karlheinz Dorn also signed an agreement under which EMAPHOS will supply CFB with its needs in purified phosphoric acid for the next 25 years.
CFB will end production of the acid in its own plant at Budenheim, Germany, the statement said.
Supplies from Morocco will come from a new unit located in Jorf Lasfar, 130 km (80 miles) south of Casablanca which is expected to start operating in July 1997.
OCP said the "agreements add more strength to the various synergies among the three partners and extend OCP'S international alliances into a new, high value added and advanced technology activity."
It said CFB was owned by the private German group OETKER whose turnover exceeded $3 billion in 1995 from its businesses which included fine chemicals, food products, sea transport and banking.
